title: Decide whether a style can be set on one copy without detaching it
goal: Today a saved text style cannot be set on the words inside a copy of a component. The app now says so plainly and offers the two moves that work, but the person who dragged the style there usually wanted THIS one button to look different, and both moves are bigger than that: setting it on the original changes every copy, and detaching gives up following the original for good. Whether one copy should be allowed to wear its own text style is a question about what a copy is, and it is the user's call.
notes: Comes out of the wording fix landed 2026-09-09 (Sources/PhotonzCore/TextStyleDrop.swift, CopyPiece). A copy can already own its colour, its size, its room, its opacity and its wording; a text style would be one more of the same family, but styles are the one thing that reach a copy from OUTSIDE the component (the Library shelf), so it is not obviously the same shape. Building it means a new kind of instance override plus a way back on the panel, so it should not start before the card is answered.
acceptance: A decision card is on the dashboard with the options written in terms of what a person sees and does
The answer is written into this task before any code is written
If the answer is yes, a style let go on the words inside a copy sets that copy alone and the copy says it has a look of its own
If the answer is no, nothing about the refusal changes and this task is retired

log.note: waiting on the decision card: should one copy be able to wear its own text style
decision "Should one copy of a component be able to wear its own text style?" resolved: A copy can wear its own style
the card was already answered on 2026-09-09: "A copy can wear its own style". Nothing to block on, so this run built it.

adversarial review before building. (1) The mock-free question was whether to make this a KNOB like every other per-copy fact; rejected, because a knob is exposed by the original and a style arrives from outside the component in one gesture, often onto a copy whose original somebody else drew, so there is nobody to ask first. Honesty comes instead from the copy saying its type is its own with a one press way back. (2) Cut the "ask which you meant" dialog (option c) as the decision did: a question in the middle of a drag is a stop. (3) Kept the refusal for a copy inside a copy, where an answer has nowhere to live, rather than taking the drop and quietly dropping it. (4) Shortest version: one record on the copy, applied in the same sync that applies every other answer, one row on the panel, no new flag.

core landed: ComponentPieceTextStyle.swift (record + set/clear/label/applyTextStyle), applied in resolvedChildren after the knob answers, cleared on detach and when an original is gone, refreshed when a style is edited or deleted. GroupContent.pieceTextStyles only written to the file when a copy has one. 16 new tests in ComponentPieceTextStyleTests, 5 more in TextStyleDropTests.

app landed: the canvas drop reaches the words inside a copy and lands on them, the sentence reads "Sets Label in Heading on this copy only", and the Component section carries an "Its own type" row with the same u-turn button "Its own size" and "Its own look" have.

adversarial review of the built thing, on the probe: the first run put "Updated 1 copy of Button" on screen after a drop on one copy, which is the app repeating your own action back at you. Fixed: a drop that landed entirely inside copies announces nothing, a drop on the original's words still does.
